discovery: Circuit quantum electrodynamics: strong coupling of single microwave photons to superconducting artificial atoms
subfield: Condensed matter / quantum optics: superconducting quantum circuits
motivation: In 2004 Blais and co-workers proposed, and Wallraff, Schoelkopf and colleagues demonstrated, the strong coupling of a single microwave photon in a superconducting transmission-line resonator to a superconducting qubit. This brought cavity quantum electrodynamics onto a chip, with coupling strengths far beyond those of atomic systems. Circuit QED opened a new regime of light-matter interaction: photon-number splitting, single-photon generation, quantum non-demolition dispersive readout, and later the ultrastrong-coupling regime. It is also the architecture behind essentially every superconducting quantum processor today. Qubits are coupled through resonator buses, read out dispersively and protected by bosonic codes. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in Josephson circuits. Circuit QED is the separate, decisive step that turned these circuits into a controllable quantum optics platform and a scalable quantum technology. It is clean, widely reproduced, and has transformed both fundamental physics and engineering.
